articles.title: Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster Plays a Bit Like a Stealthy Hollow Knight | IGN Preview
articles.summary: I had a maniacally delightful time with the very small slice of Warhammer Age of Sigmar: Deathmaster I got to chew on. The art style is gloomy and grimy while remaining very readable. The mixture of stealth game mainstays with Hollow Knight-stye platforming clicks together pretty seamlessly.
body: Vihneek's starting surroundings are gory, putrid, and almost hopeless. Which is to say, absolutely perfect for a game starring the Skaven, with layered caverns stretching off into the background and every crevice and torn canvas painted with a gloomy malice. I'm not a huge expert on Age of Sigmar lore, but coming from a Warhammer Fantasy background, I wouldn't have necessarily been able to tell this was a different setting. The Skaven are still quite recognizably Skaven, in all their duplicitous glory, doing Skaven things like sneaking and scheming through an underground world ruled over by many clans who often engage in bitter rivalries.

articles.title: After 10 Years, Pokémon Go is Getting a Pokémon Anime Crossover Episode
articles.summary: The world of Pokémon Go will cross over into the Pokémon anime series later this month, in an episode where the gang meet Professor Willow and spin a PokéStop. Pokémon Go celebrated its 10th anniversary this summer, and the celebrations will continue this month as a landmark episode of the Pokémon…
body: Yes, Professor Willow himself will be making his anime debut, leaping over from his role assisting players in Pokémon Go. Coming along with him is Meltan, his partner Pokémon, and at least one PokéStop — the identifiers of real-world locations that Pokémon Go players spin in-game.

In a trailer posted today by the official Japanese Pokémon social media account, above Captain Pikachu can be seen spinning the PokéStop, accurately recieving Pokéballs and berries as a reward. And in a further nod, a Kecleon is revealed to have been hiding in plain sight — a neat nod to how the chameleon-like creature can be caught in Pokémon Go.

Exactly how Professor Willow will cross paths with Roy, Liko and the series' other characters remains to be seen, as Go's canonicity with the rest of the Pokémon franchise has always been left unclear. Indeed, Meltan and Melmetal, which debuted first in Pokémon Go, lack an official region of origin (such as Johto or Kanto), and are instead listed as being discovered in an "Unidentified" place.

articles.title: You Can Watch A Cow Play Eve Online Right Now
articles.summary: Earlier this summer, Fenris Creations (formerly CCP Games) released an update to its popular online spacefaring MMO called Cradle of War, which the community immediately abbreviated to "CoW." This shorthand apparently sparked a few ideas inside Fenris, and now an actual cow is livestreaming an Eve…
body: The cow, whose name is Valva and username is FC CapitalCowPilot, is manning a mining ship on a deep space mining operation. The team at Fenris Creations fitted its pen with "cow-proof" buttons, which when stepped on will perform certain in-game actions, while a voiceover host delivers cow facts to viewers of the livestream.

As of this writing, over 200 players have joined CapitalCowPilot's mining expedition, with over 4000 viewers watching along on Twitch as the cow moves around its pen. Fenris Creations has announced some community goals which can be unlocked during the stream, including new skins for ships and new updates for the Cradle of War expansion.

The stream will run "for roughly 4 to 6 hours," as Fenris admits that it's "on the cow's time, she's not on ours." Valva has made quite an impression on the stream's chat, with some users demanding that the cow be left alone while on its mining mission.

The Cradle of War expansion's non-bovine additions include time-limited Military Campaigns, which let players complete tasks in order to advance their empire's goals, and a new area called Exordium specifically built to help onboard new players.

articles.title: Super Smash Bros. Ultimate Gets An Update, But Not The One You Want
articles.summary: In what feels like a monkey's paw situation, Super Smash Bros. Ultimate unexpectedly received a new patch--but unlike recent updates for other major Nintendo games, this Smash update doesn't include any Switch 2-specific features. The Ver.
body: The Ver. 13.0.5 patch for Ultimate fixes "behavior that occurs when invalid data is sent or received in online battles," according to the Nintendo Support website. It isn't clear from the patch notes (or note, rather) what "invalid data" refers to, but some users on Reddit speculated that the update targets mods.

Meanwhile, fellow Switch 1 game Mario Kart 8 Deluxe received a hefty 4.0.0 update with substantial features for Switch 2 users, including split-screen support for up to eight players, camera support, shorter loading times, and higher resolutions. Pikmin 3 Deluxe also got a similar Switch 2 update this week.

It's a disappointing time for Smash Bros. fans, with not a single hint of a new Smash game or a proper Switch 2 update for Ultimate, whether that comes in the form of a free patch or a Switch 2 Edition with new content.

articles.title: The Big Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered Interview: Launching Against GTA 6, Cutting Hedorah, and Staying (Mostly) Faithful to a GameCube Classic
articles.summary: IGN spoke with Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered senior designer Simon Strange to hear about the game fans have long pleaded for — but never thought would actually happen.
body: IGN gave Atari and Pipeworks' Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee an 8.4/10 review when it launched in 2002. At the time, we said, "as far as multiplayer experiences go, Godzilla represents one of GameCube's very best." Now, senior designer Simon Strange and the rest of the team are back and ready to do it all over again.

With remastered graphics, a playable Showa-era Mechagodzilla, and a few new irradiated bells and whistles, Godzilla: Destroy All Monsters Melee Remastered is set to arrive at a time when kaiju fans are in desperate need of a standalone game featuring the King of the Monsters. IGN spoke with Strange to learn about how things have changed since he first helped bring the original game to players in the 2000s.

articles.title: Don’t Care About GTA 6’s Romance System? Don’t Use It, Dev Says
articles.summary: GTA 6 's Jason and Lucia can be romantically involved, or they can just be partners in crime. If you're not interested in the game's romance system, don't use it, Rockstar's Rob Nelson said in a new interview. "I have to say it feels great--if you are into it as a concept.
body: Players who do wish to grow and nurture a romantic relationship between Jason and Lucia can hold hands, visit a zoo together, or enjoy a romantic stroll on the beach, Nelson said. If players don’t want to do those things, they don’t have to, but Nelson said players might miss out on other things.

"I don’t want to say too much more about this because I don’t want to spoil anything. It really adds a compelling element to things, and it’s one of the reasons we wanted to approach this sort of story, because it's completely different for us," Nelson said. "Could we bring some sort of emotional resonance to GTA for people if they wanted to engage with it? Could we also provide mechanisms for people to just opt out of it if they're not into it? If they feel like, ‘I don't want a relationship in this?’ That's what we're going to find out. It's not something that we want to foist upon players."
Nelson said players might grow to "feel protective of [Jason and Lucia] as a unit" as they progress through the game, and the developers at Rockstar didn't originally envision this.

articles.title: LOTR Fans Need To “Be Patient,” Kingdom Come Dev Says About New Middle-earth RPG
articles.summary: Kingdom Come developer Warhorse is working on multiple new games, including a The Lord of the Rings role-playing game. We don't know much about it right now, and Warhorse isn't likely to share more details anytime soon.
body: In a post on social media, Warhorse said, "We're excited to tell you guys more, you've just gotta be patient for now." In short, you should be more like an Ent and slow down. Good things come to those who wait, after all.
Warhorse announced the game earlier this year, saying it will be a "deeply immersive" open-world Middle-earth RPG.

The game will feature a “living world” populated by “interesting characters, memorable places, and, of course, a strong narrative focus," the developers said. This doesn't tell us much about it, but it’s a starting point for understanding where the game may be headed. We also know that Deliverance 2 design director Viktor Bocan is leading the development of the untitled Lord of the Rings game.
In addition to the new Lord of the Rings game, Warhorse is producing a new Kingdom Come game, along with a Kingdom Come movie.

articles.title: LEGO Advent Calendars for 2026 Are Already on Sale
articles.summary: Here’s an early Christmas surprise. The 2026 editions of the LEGO advent calendars just came out on September 1, but Walmart already has them deeply discounted. You can get the Marvel, Star Wars, and Disney calendars for $35 each, down from $45.
body: It’s anyone’s guess how long this deal will last, so grab it quick if you want it, even though you’ll have to wait three months to open the first mini-build.

This year, the licensed advent calendars cover Star Wars, Marvel, and Disney Princesses – notably missing is Harry Potter. These are on sale for $35 each, down from an MSRP of $45. (Note: Walmart has them listed at $59.99, but that's not the MSRP shown on the official LEGO Store or Amazon ). Then there are calendars based on the LEGO-made themes Friends and City. These are on sale for $25 each, down from $35.

Advent calendars, for those who don’t know, are meant to help kids (or adults!) count down the days to Christmas. Every day between December 1 - 24, you open one small perforated door on the LEGO box to reveal a tiny compartment containing a LEGO micro-build. Each day’s build comes in a bag and is made of just a handful of pieces. On the inside of the door flap you’ll find a simple diagram showing how to assemble the build.

articles.title: One 23-year-old Magic Card Protects a Popular Hobbit Commander From Total Annihilation
articles.summary: Imagine this: Your Commander is a skin-changer from Middle-earth who's assumed the form of a massive black bear. He leads an army of lesser bears — infusing them with extra bear power so they grow stronger — into battle.
body: Beorn the Fierce is one of the most popular Commanders from Magic ’s latest The Hobbit crossover set, with 4,410 decks registered on EDHREC as of this writing. The five-mana 6/6 has trample and gives every other bear you control +2/+2. At the beginning of combat, he gives a trample counter that also gives them the bear type. If you control at least three bears after that, you draw two cards.

Commanders with both inherent combat tricks and a draw engine often become hugely popular, and Beorn is no exception. He’s arguably one of the very best Commanders ever for a bear typal or kindred deck that focuses on bear-typed creatures. Where he’s lacking, however, is in protection, especially because filling up your board with a ton of bears makes you vulnerable to board wipes. That’s where Caller of the Claw comes in.

Originally released in 2003’s Legions, Caller of the Claw is a three-mana 2/2 elf with flash. (You know it’s old because the original printing describes the flash effect before it became a named ability.) When it enters the battlefield, you create a 2/2 green bear creature token for every nontoken creature put into your graveyard from the battlefield that turn.

articles.title: Monster Hunter Is About to Change Forever
articles.summary: Monster Hunter Wilds is getting significant changes next year with the Ascendance expansion, which Capcom has described as a “massive” update. The DLC will introduce a new region called the Eastlands, along with a fresh lineup of monsters to hunt that includes elder dragons.
body: An overview video showcases how Boost Bracer works, and many players are likening it to Nero ’s moveset in Devil May Cry. Players build up Boost Bracer energy by staying aggressive, filling up a meter shown at the bottom of the screen. Once you’ve built up enough meter, you can use a Boost Driver attack to activate Boost, a powered-up mode that strengthens existing attacks and adds all-new moves. Basically, as long as you’re in Boost, every weapon becomes better at what it’s designed to do: dual blades become faster, shields become bulkier, and the bow gets a stagger-inducing finisher.

All 14 weapons will receive new abilities linked to Boost, and Capcom is releasing videos detailing the updates for each. The Greatsword got a video showcasing its ability to chain together offset counters to deal with multiple powerful attacks in a row. Additionally, it looks like this already hard-hitting weapon will pack even more of a punch, with the Boosted Greatsword landing stagger after stagger.

articles.title: Square Enix denies it's going private following Japanese reports to the contrary
articles.summary: Square Enix, the Japanese publisher and developer behind Final Fantasy, Kingdom Hearts, Dragon Quest and many other legendary franchises, has had to release a statement to quash claims it's going private.
body: Square Enix's statement was issued in response to a report in Japanese business magazine Sentaku, which claimed the Japanese publisher was exploring the possibility of going private, and had interest from foreign investment funds. The report boosted the value of Square Enix's stock price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange by seven-to-12 percent yesterday.

"The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix Holdings Co., LTD. (the 'Company') going private. However, this information was not announced by the Company," Square Enix said in a statement published on the same day. "No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."

As to where this rumour of Square Enix going private began, Investing.com reported that major shareholder 3D Investment Partners, which holds around 18.5 percent of Square Enix's shares, may have been a factor in the speculation. The investment firm previously criticised Square Enix's management plan, calling on the board of directors to reassess the company's strategy.

articles.title: Magic’s Successful Print-To-Demand Secret Lair Drops Are Sticking Around
articles.summary: Last month, Magic: The Gathering 's Secret Lair tried something new with the release of a Hatsune Miku Commander deck. To address persistent issues of highly coveted drops selling out almost immediately, the Miku deck introduced a 24-hour limited order window.
body: In an official post on the Magic: The Gathering blog, Hodgins expanded by saying the drop "did exactly the job we wanted it to do. If you ordered inside the window, you're getting a deck. That's the whole point, and it's the part I'm happiest about." The new 24-hour limited order window is largely meant to make it easier for players to get their hands on decks that have a unique combination of high demand and out-of-the-box playability. The new policy was tested out with the Miku deck following negative feedback about the Goblin Storm and Dandân drops, which sold out almost immediately.

Going forward, Secret Lair is going to keep experimenting with the 24-hour limited order window. That will happen in a matter of weeks with Secret Lair Commander Deck: Odds and Ends. Hodgins says news about that will be shared in the near future. He also teases that a dedicated storefront for Secret Lair drops could be coming in the future to make the purchase process more streamlined and transparent for customers. Secret Lair will use the Odds and Ends drop as another chance to gather data to inform future 24-hour releases and the design of a dedicated storefront.

articles.title: The Definitive ’70s Action Blockbuster Is Officially Streaming for Free on YouTube
articles.summary: Before CGI sanded the edges off modern blockbusters, the 1970s martial arts boom delivered a completely different kind of cinematic thrill: pure, unadulterated human kinetics. Watching such films today is a masterclass in the anatomy of action.
body: Nowhere is that raw, pioneering genius more fiercely realized than in 1972’s The Way of the Dragon. Arguably Bruce Lee’s finest hour, the film still serves as the clearest, most unfiltered glimpse into the visionary auteur he was destined to become at the time. Lee crafted a kinetic masterpiece, culminating in what might be the single greatest one-on-one fight ever committed to celluloid. Fortunately, you don't have to hunt down a Blu-ray to experience the impact. The Way of the Dragon is currently streaming for free on YouTube, making it the perfect time to witness the master at the absolute height of his powers.

For his directorial debut, Lee refused to ease into the driver’s seat. Instead, he hijacked the entire production. Writing, producing, directing, choreographing, and starring in The Way of the Dragon, Lee seized an unprecedented level of creative control. The result is a film that actively defies the established martial arts template. Beyond the blistering combat, Lee injects the narrative with broad fish-out-of-water comedy, genuine romance, and a swaggering personality that previous martial arts movies sorely lacked.

articles.title: World of Warcraft fans so eager to find confirmation of "Classic Plus", they've dug "wow 2" evidence out of Blizzards' backend
articles.summary: World of Warcraft fans are currently obsessing over colours, as dataminers pull hues from Blizzard's website that are labelled under a curious "wow 2" tag. This, some believe, could be an indication of a major reveal at next week's BlizzCon event.
body: As detailed on a World of Warcraft Classic Reddit post, dataminers delved into Blizzard's websites CSS (cascading style sheet) where various visual assets could be found in code form. Within this code, the "wow 2" tag was found and the colour codes.

These colours, a spread of mostly blue shades accompanied by a light red, brown, and white, vary drastically from colours assigned to existing tags in World of Warcraft, World of Warcraft; Midnight (the current retail expansion), Diablo, Overwatch, and so on. As such, it appears these colours are attached to a new project at Blizzard - one that has been added to the website ahead of this weekend's BlizzCon.

As for what this "wow 2" tag could be, the best bet is the much-speculated "World of Warcraft Camelot", or as it's better known, "Classic Plus". It is widely believed this is an updated or expanded version of World of Warcraft Classic - the original version of the MMO. This is similar to how Jagex built upon the original 2007 version of RuneScape with Old School RuneScape, and to how Blizzard is now expanding Diablo 2.

articles.title: September's first wave of Xbox Game Pass games revealed, and it brings RuneScape to console for the first time
articles.summary: The first wave of games coming to PC and Xbox Game Pass in September have been revealed, and it's a little barren. Probably the highlight is the arrival of new RuneScape co-op survival game Dragonwilds.
body: Dragonwilds' arrival is quietly a rather monumental moment for RuneScape, for it represents the first time a RuneScape game has appeared on console. But to be clear: this is not the age-old MMO, it's a brand new open-world survival crafting game in the vein of Valheim or Enshrouded - that kind of thing.

Dragonwilds has been in early access testing since last spring, so this day-one Game Pass launch on 15th September represents its full 1.0 release, and it seems to have had pretty good feedback so far. Steam reviews for Dragonwilds are "very positive", and Lottie - our resident RuneScape super-nerd, she won't mind me saying - was very encouraged when she previewed RuneScape: Dragonwilds last year. Dragonwilds is coming to Game Pass Ultimate, Premium, and PC by the way.

You might also find competitive co-op platformer SpeedRunners 2 of interest - the original had a good reception on Steam - and the delightfully dawn medieval roguelike deck-builder The Royal Writ, which was released late last summer on PC. That is unless you fancy playing six-year-old Call of Duty game Black Ops Cold War? No? Didn't think so.
